title: `SubtweenTweener::step` processes delta incorrectly
body: ### Tested versions v4.4.1.stable.custom_build [d91ae7f7e] ### System information Godot v4.4.1.stable (d91ae7f7e) - Windows 11 (build 26100) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2070 SUPER (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.6603) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-10700F CPU @ 2.90GHz (16 threads) ### Issue description This code in SubtweenTweener::step does not process delta correctly: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/8aa37cab8950351d96f541581abdc42136283f24/scene/animation/tween.cpp#L899-L903 It's broken in two ways: 1. `subtween->step(r_delta)` returns true even when the subtween completes, so the if statement needs to actually be checking `!subtween->is_running()` 2. The math with `r_delta` checks out if `subtween->get_total_time()` reflected the true length of the subtween. However, the subtween's `total_time` is influenced by the same delta used to calculate `elapsed_time`. This means that `elapsed_time` will always be equivalent to the subtween's `total_time`, and therefore `r_delta` will always be set to 0. According to documentation, this is intended behavior: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/8aa37cab8950351d96f541581abdc42136283f24/doc/classes/Tween.xml#L143-L144 This could be fixed by making `get_total_time()` accurate to the time elapsed within a tween by making the change in this screenshot (though this is a behavior change that causes the NOTE in the above documentation to become inaccurate): --- This distinction leads to incorrect behavior in subtween steps -- essentially, delta does not carry through when a SubtweenTweeners completes in the same frame as its step, causing the Tweener to pause for a frame after subtweens at best, or completely breaking custom steps at worst. ### Steps to reproduce The MRP is a test scene with several tool buttons that shows the difference between running a tween that uses multiple subtweens VS. attempting to skip through them using `custom_step`. Applying the fixes described above results in correct behavior, though I'm unsure if we're comfortable changing how `get_total_time()` returns, even if it leads to an (arguably) more accurate result. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [subtween_step_bug_2025-08-13_15-46-38.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/21762171/subtween_step_bug_2025-08-13_15-46-38.zip)
